glossary.description: The lab's metrics and business terms from the dbt semantic layer, linked to the columns of bet_kcmax (synthetic data; issue 360).

terms.description: Distinct customers with any site or CRM action in the period asked. Metric acting_customers: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM bet_kcmax.customer_actions, dated by event_date.
Clicks on ads across campaigns. Metric ad_clicks: SUM(clicks) FROM bet_kcmax.ad_spend, dated by spend_date.
Ad spend across campaigns, in EUR. Metric ad_spend_eur: SUM(spend) FROM bet_kcmax.ad_spend, dated by spend_date.
Candidates who applied, on the day they applied (one application per candidate). Metric applications: COUNT(candidate_id) FROM bet_kcmax.applications, dated by applied_date.

Average amount of a non-cancelled order (revenue over non-cancelled orders, over the whole period asked, never an average of daily averages). Metric average_order_value_eur: revenue_eur / orders_total (where status <> 'cancelled'), each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).
Value of the bookings made, in EUR. Metric booking_value_eur: SUM(amount) FROM bet_kcmax.bookings, dated by booked_date.
Bookings made by leads, on the day they were made. Metric bookings: COUNT(*) FROM bet_kcmax.bookings, dated by booked_date.

Bookings from the first of the month up to and including each day (month to date); group by metric_time__day and read the day asked. Grouped by week or month it is the count up to that period's last day. Metric bookings_mtd: bookings month to date.

Bookings' change from the week before, as a share of that week's bookings (0.10 is 10 % more); group by metric_time__week to compare whole weeks. Empty where either week has no bookings. Metric bookings_wow_growth: (bookings - bookings_prior_week) * 1.0 / nullif(bookings_prior_week, 0), where bookings_prior_week is bookings 1 week earlier.

Model-derived: calls labelled by gemini-3.5-flash (in the lab, recorded from an OpenRouter free model) under prompt v1, on the day of the call; group by call__topic for calls by topic. The build holds the labels to kappa 0.6 to 0.7 per signal on the golden set (silver.call_label_agreement). Metric calls_labelled: COUNT(transcript_id) FROM bet_kcmax.call_signals, dated by call_date.

Model-derived: calls in which the customer raised an objection (price, timing or a competitor), labelled by gemini-3.5-flash (in the lab, recorded from an OpenRouter free model) under prompt v1; objection labels agree with the golden set at kappa 0.6 or more. Metric calls_with_objection: COUNT(transcript_id) FROM bet_kcmax.call_signals WHERE objection <> 'none', dated by call_date.
Share of orders cancelled. Metric cancellation_rate: orders_cancelled / orders_total, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).

Candidates who had applied by the end of each day, counted per day; grouped by candidate__stage (or filtered on it) it is the number in each hiring stage at the end of that day, from the stage history. Ask it per day: over a longer period it counts the candidates who were in the stage on any of its days. Metric candidates_in_stage: COUNT(DISTINCT candidate_id) FROM bet_kcmax.candidate_days, dated by calendar_date.

Site sessions with an add to cart, on the day of the add to cart. Metric cart_sessions: COUNT(DISTINCT case when action_type = 'add_to_cart' then session_id end) FROM bet_kcmax.customer_actions, dated by event_date.

Share of site sessions with an add to cart that checked out on the add to cart's day or the day after, counted on the add to cart's day. Metric cart_to_checkout_rate: share of cart_sessions (where action_type = 'add_to_cart') whose session reaches checkout_sessions within 2 days, counted on the cart_sessions date.

Site sessions with a checkout, on the day of the checkout. Metric checkout_sessions: COUNT(DISTINCT case when action_type = 'checkout' then session_id end) FROM bet_kcmax.customer_actions, dated by event_date.

Ad spend divided by bookings over the whole period asked (total spend over total bookings, never an average of daily ratios); the one definition of cost per conversion. Metric cost_per_booking_eur: ad_spend_eur / bookings, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).

Ad spend divided by leads over the whole period asked (total spend over total leads, never an average of daily ratios); the one definition of cost per lead. Metric cost_per_lead_eur: ad_spend_eur / leads, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).

Site and CRM actions, on the day they happened; group by customer_action__action_type for actions per type. Metric customer_actions: COUNT(event_id) FROM bet_kcmax.customer_actions, dated by event_date.
Distinct customers with at least one non-cancelled order. Metric customers_distinct: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM bet_kcmax.orders WHERE status <> 'cancelled', dated by order_date.
All customers who had signed up by each day, a running total over all time; grouped by week or month it is the count on that period's last day. Metric customers_to_date: signups all time to date.

Share of returns whose reason was damaged goods (damaged returns over all returns, both counted on the returned order's date, over the whole period asked). Metric damaged_return_share: returns_on_order_date (where reason = 'damaged') / returns_on_order_date, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).

Distinct customers with any site or CRM action in the 28 days ending on the day (that day and the 27 before); monthly engaged customers. Metric engaged_customers_28d: acting_customers over the 28 days ending on each day.

Distinct customers with any site or CRM action in the 7 days ending on the day (that day and the 6 before); weekly engaged customers. Metric engaged_customers_7d: acting_customers over the 7 days ending on each day.
Candidates hired, on the day they were hired. Metric hires: COUNT(candidate_id) FROM bet_kcmax.applications WHERE current_stage = 'hired', dated by hired_date.

Share of leads that booked within 30 days of being created, counted on the lead's creation day. Metric lead_to_booking_rate: share of leads whose lead reaches bookings within 30 days, counted on the leads date.
CRM leads created, on the day they were created. Metric leads: COUNT(*) FROM bet_kcmax.leads, dated by created_date.

Leads from the first of the month up to and including each day (month to date); group by metric_time__day and read the day asked. Grouped by week or month it is the count up to that period's last day. Metric leads_mtd: leads month to date.

Leads' change from the week before, as a share of that week's leads (0.10 is 10 % more); group by metric_time__week to compare whole weeks. Empty where either week has no leads. Metric leads_wow_growth: (leads - leads_prior_week) * 1.0 / nullif(leads_prior_week, 0), where leads_prior_week is leads 1 week earlier.

BigQuery only: the median amount of a non-cancelled order, BigQuery's approximate continuous percentile (APPROX_QUANTILES); Postgres has no rendering of it, so an agent on Postgres declines. Metric median_order_value_eur: PERCENTILE_CONT(amount, 0.5) FROM bet_kcmax.orders WHERE status <> 'cancelled', dated by order_date.

Outreach messages that got a reply, on the day the message was sent; grows as late replies arrive. Metric messages_replied: COUNT(first_replied_ts) FROM bet_kcmax.outreach_messages, dated by sent_date.
Outreach messages sent to partner contacts, on the day they were sent. Metric messages_sent: COUNT(message_id) FROM bet_kcmax.outreach_messages, dated by sent_date.
Revenue minus partner returns (finance's net sales). Metric net_revenue_eur: coalesce(revenue_eur, 0) - coalesce(returns_eur, 0).

Model-derived: share of labelled calls in which the customer raised an objection (calls with an objection over calls labelled, over the whole period asked), labelled by gemini-3.5-flash (in the lab, recorded from an OpenRouter free model) under prompt v1; objection labels agree with the golden set at kappa 0.6 or more. Metric objection_rate: calls_with_objection / calls_labelled, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).
Orders with status cancelled. Metric orders_cancelled: COUNT(order_id) FROM bet_kcmax.orders WHERE status = 'cancelled', dated by order_date.
All orders placed, cancelled included. Metric orders_total: COUNT(*) FROM bet_kcmax.orders, dated by order_date.
Distinct partners with at least one reply from their contacts in the period asked. Metric partners_engaged: COUNT(DISTINCT partner_id) FROM bet_kcmax.outreach_replies, dated by replied_date.

Model-derived: calls the customer ended in a positive mood, labelled by gemini-3.5-flash (in the lab, recorded from an OpenRouter free model) under prompt v1; sentiment labels agree with the golden set at kappa 0.5 or more. Metric positive_calls: COUNT(transcript_id) FROM bet_kcmax.call_signals WHERE sentiment = 'positive', dated by call_date.

Model-derived: share of labelled calls the customer ended in a positive mood (positive calls over calls labelled, over the whole period asked), labelled by gemini-3.5-flash (in the lab, recorded from an OpenRouter free model) under prompt v1; sentiment labels agree with the golden set at kappa 0.5 or more. Metric positive_sentiment_share: positive_calls / calls_labelled, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).

Budget left in the month, in EUR: each campaign's last snapshot in the period asked (never a sum across days), added up over campaigns; by month it is what was left at month end. Metric remaining_budget_eur: SUM(remaining_eur) FROM bet_kcmax.campaign_budgets, dated by snapshot_date.

Distinct customers with a non-cancelled order in the period who have placed two or more orders in all (repeat customers). Metric repeat_customers: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM bet_kcmax.orders WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND orders_total per customer >= 2, dated by order_date.

Share of revenue that came from repeat customers (revenue from customers with two or more orders in all over revenue, over the whole period asked). Metric repeat_revenue_share: revenue_repeat_customers_eur / revenue_eur, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).
Replies to outreach messages, on the day they arrived. Metric replies: COUNT(reply_id) FROM bet_kcmax.outreach_replies, dated by replied_date.

Share of outreach messages that got a reply, counted on the day the message was sent, so a day's rate rises as late replies arrive (messages replied over messages sent for the whole period asked, never replies over messages of the same day); the one definition of reply rate and response rate. Metric reply_rate: messages_replied / messages_sent, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).

Share of orders that were returned (returns over orders, both counted on the day the order was placed, over the whole period asked); a return in October of a September order counts against September. Metric return_rate: returns_on_order_date / orders_total, each totalled over the whole period asked (a ratio of totals, never an average of daily ratios).
Number of partner returns. Metric returns_count: COUNT(return_id) FROM bet_kcmax.returns, dated by return_date.
Sum of partner return amounts. Metric returns_eur: SUM(amount) FROM bet_kcmax.returns, dated by return_date.

Number of partner returns, counted on the day the returned order was placed rather than the day of the return; the return rate's numerator. Metric returns_on_order_date: COUNT(*) FROM bet_kcmax.returns, dated by order_date.
Sum of amount for non-cancelled orders (the one definition of revenue). Metric revenue_eur: SUM(amount) FROM bet_kcmax.orders WHERE status <> 'cancelled', dated by order_date.

Revenue from the first of the month up to and including each day (month to date); group by metric_time__day and read the day asked. Grouped by week or month it is the total up to that period's last day. Metric revenue_eur_mtd: revenue_eur month to date.

Revenue's change from the week before, as a share of that week's revenue (0.10 is 10 % more); group by metric_time__week to compare whole weeks, by metric_time__day to compare a day with the same weekday a week earlier. Empty where either week has no revenue. Metric revenue_eur_wow_growth: (revenue_eur - revenue_eur_prior_week) / nullif(revenue_eur_prior_week, 0), where revenue_eur_prior_week is revenue_eur 1 week earlier.

Revenue (non-cancelled orders) from repeat customers, those who have placed two or more orders in all. Metric revenue_repeat_customers_eur: SUM(amount) FROM bet_kcmax.orders WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND orders_total per customer >= 2, dated by order_date.

Share of customers who placed their first order within 30 days of signing up (the signup day and the 29 after it), counted on the signup day; by signup month, the share of that cohort. Metric signup_to_first_order_rate: share of signups whose customer reaches orders_total within 30 days, counted on the signups date.
Customers who signed up, counted on the day they signed up (new customers). Metric signups: COUNT(*) FROM bet_kcmax.customers, dated by signup_date.
Site sessions with a page view, on the day of the page view. Metric site_sessions: COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) FROM bet_kcmax.customer_actions WHERE action_type = 'page_view', dated by event_date.

Average days from applying to being hired over the candidates hired in the period asked, on the day they were hired; the one definition of time to hire and days to hire. Metric time_to_hire_days: AVG(days_to_hire) FROM bet_kcmax.applications WHERE current_stage = 'hired', dated by hired_date.

Share of site sessions with a page view that added to cart on the page view's day or the day after, counted on the page view's day. Metric view_to_cart_rate: share of site_sessions whose session reaches cart_sessions within 2 days, counted on the site_sessions date.

Where a candidate is in hiring: applied, screen, interview, offer, then hired, or rejected at any stage before hired. A candidate's stage on a day is the one they were in at the end of that day, from the stage history the warehouse snapshots after every load, so two changes between loads keep the later. Also called: pipeline stage, recruitment stage, candidate status, funnel stage. Metrics: candidates_in_stage.

A lead that books. Bookings count conversions on the day they are made; the lead-to-booking rate counts a lead as converted when it books within 30 days of being created; cost per conversion is cost per booking. Also called: converted lead, booked lead. Metrics: bookings, lead_to_booking_rate, cost_per_booking_eur.

A value a language model read out of free text (a call's topic, objection, sentiment, next step), not a value a system recorded. It comes from a versioned prompt, is scored against a golden set of calls whose true labels are known, and a build fails below the agreed agreement; a metric over it says so in its description. Filter on the prompt version to compare two versions. Also called: AI label, call signal, model label, extracted signal. Dimensions: call__prompt_version, call__topic, call__objection, call__sentiment, call__next_step.

The marketing channel a campaign runs on: search, social, display, email or partner. Leads and bookings take their campaign's channel; a booking whose lead is not loaded yet has none. Also called: marketing channel, acquisition channel. Metrics: ad_spend_eur, leads, bookings, cost_per_lead_eur, cost_per_booking_eur. Dimensions: campaign__channel.

The ISO-2 country a campaign targets. It can differ from a lead's own country and a customer's country, so spend, leads and bookings by market group by the campaign, not the person. Also called: target market, campaign country. Metrics: ad_spend_eur, leads, bookings. Dimensions: campaign__market.

A customer with any site or CRM action (a page view, a cart, a checkout, an email opened, a support contact) in the trailing window ending on the day: 7 days for weekly, 28 for monthly. It is not an active customer, which counts customers who placed a non-cancelled order. Also called: weekly active customers, monthly active customers, WAU, MAU, engaged users. Metrics: engaged_customers_7d, engaged_customers_28d.

The steps a site session walks: page view, then add to cart, then checkout. A step's rate counts the sessions that took the next step on the same day as the step before or the day after, on the day of the step before. Also called: conversion funnel, checkout funnel, cart conversion. Metrics: site_sessions, cart_sessions, checkout_sessions, view_to_cart_rate, cart_to_checkout_rate.

The customers who signed up in the same calendar month. A metric by cohort groups by the month its customer signed up, not the month the order was placed. Also called: cohort, acquisition cohort. Metrics: orders_total, revenue_eur, customers_distinct, signups. Dimensions: customer__signup_date.

The customer's ISO-2 country. It is not the market a campaign targets nor a lead's country, so revenue, net revenue, returns or orders by country group by it. Also called: country. Metrics: orders_total, revenue_eur, customers_distinct, returns_eur, net_revenue_eur. Dimensions: customer__country.

Ambiguous on its own: customers can mean signups (customers who signed up in the period), active customers (distinct customers with a non-cancelled order in the period) or customers to date (everyone signed up by a day). When the question does not say which, ask which one is meant or give each, named. Also called: customer count, number of customers, our customers. Metrics: signups, customers_distinct, customers_to_date.

Where an order stands: placed, shipped or cancelled. A cancelled order counts in orders and the cancellation rate, never in revenue or active customers. Also called: cancelled order, shipped order, placed order. Metrics: orders_total, orders_cancelled, cancellation_rate, revenue_eur, customers_distinct. Dimensions: order__status.

Ambiguous on its own: sales can mean revenue (gross, the non-cancelled orders' amounts) or net revenue (revenue minus partner returns, finance's net sales). When the question does not say gross or net, ask which one is meant or give both, named. Also called: turnover, takings. Metrics: revenue_eur, net_revenue_eur.

A partner at least one of whose contacts replied to an outreach message in the period asked. A reply to a message sent before the first loaded day counts as a reply but names no partner. Also called: responsive partners, partners who replied, active partners. Metrics: partners_engaged.

An order a partner reports as returned, with the amount and the partner's reason, on the UTC day it was recorded. Returns lower net revenue; revenue itself keeps the order. Also called: return. Metrics: returns_eur, returns_count, net_revenue_eur. Dimensions: return__reason.
